newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes stable to higher, eyes on IOC tender.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes stable to higher, eyes on IOC tender.

text.p: Crude oil prices in Asia were stable to slightly higher on Friday with Minas premiums stretched further on strong China demand.
China has supported the Indonesian grades throughout the January trading months. Traders said China's low stock position was exacerbated by buying ahead of the Chinese New Year.
On Friday, trading sources confirmed a Japanese trader sold China 150,000 barrels of Minas at a premium of ICP 85-90 cents.
That was above a day-earlier trade at ICP plus 75 cents, although a major said it had achieved ICP +85 cents late last week.
A European trader was said to have sold the last remaining cargo of Oman into China at a premium of MPM +33 cents -- the highest premium yet for a full cargo.
Partials have been sold as high as +35 cents but the last full cargo was said sold at +25/26.

However, some traders said the European trader may have sold a Feb cargo and a March cargo back-to-back at a premium in the low 20s to account for the expected lower Chinese demand heading into March.
Trading in Middle East grades was quiet with focus shifting to the Indian tender for February crude.
Traders said 10 Dubai cargoes were offered into the tender at first-half month quotes +63 to +72 cents. A major offered at $1.00 premium, which could be against full month quotes.
The last spot Dubai sold was a trader to a South Korean refinery at full-month quotes plus 93 cents, traders said.
A producer sold 200,000 barrels of Tapis at quotes plus $1.35, up 15 cents from the previous deal for a small parcel.

A January North West Shelf cargo of 500,000 barrels was sold at Arun quotes plus 80 cents and a January Cossack at Tapis quotes plus 40 cents -- both higher than recent deals. --Singapore, N Fullick, (+65 870 3081), Tokyo, M Yoshikawa (+813 5473 3706)
